contracts.requirement: Spec creation/removal, fields/time samples, ordered lists and conflict cases, batching/diff application, semantic correctness against independent models, valid OMPF/no-op fixtures, malformed FlatBuffers/bounds/overflow, URI property tests; no oracle derived from a client implementation

Repeated writes to one field, dictionary key or time sample in a log compile to one record of the last value, including across a move of the identity they address but never across an erase or onto a recreated identity, against the stock oracle and with the operation and entry limits counting the collapsed records and the log operation limit refusing a longer log before any per-operation work; the coalesced host turns that reach the compiler are outside these cases. Public creation/CreateNew/live Export, graph-service value families outside that profile (quaternions, half, unsigned and 64-bit integers, bool and integer arrays, asset paths, other Gf vectors and matrices, ranges, dictionaries, list operations other than paths, non-UTF-8 or NUL-holding strings and nonfinite scalar doubles), many-writer fuzz/shrinking, supported-host concurrency and full product qualification remain open.

contracts.requirement: Each layer write and creation carries one operation ID; an unknown outcome is re-sent once with the same ID, bytes and writer ID, only on an endpoint whose replies have shown operation-ID support (an UNSPECIFIED reply to an identified request clears it), while the write stays in flight; an APPLIED or ALREADY_COMMITTED reply settles it even when its sequence is below positions the read has passed; an UNSPECIFIED reply or a second unknown outcome leaves OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and a definitive rejection is final, with edits kept
contracts.coverage_limit: Qualified only against the reference service's model of the operation-ID contract, which the deployed Live Edit service does not yet implement. The creation cases mark their endpoint through a driver seam, because a creation is its driver endpoint's first write. The ordering of a peer commit read before the re-send's reply is deterministic only in the native progress test.

contracts.requirement: On an endpoint whose Ping reports operation IDs and chained writes, a layer issues chained writes, each with a ChainedUpdateLayerHeader, in FIFO order within a window that starts at 8, grows by one per window of acknowledgments without a refusal, halves on a refusal that applied nothing and stays within 1 to 16; each write's predecessor is fixed at admission, empty for the writer's first write to the object, and a layer's first write to an object its endpoint wrote before issues unchained and alone; an endpoint that does not chain writes keeps one unchained write in flight. A chained write a replica refuses INVALID_ARGUMENT without an ErrorInfo of the service's domain applied nothing: the endpoint stops chaining, later chained calls stay in flight, and writes are re-sent unchanged and unchained from the first not known to have committed, each once every chained call carrying it or an earlier write has returned and is settled, writes whose chained calls ended unsettled (cancelled, timed out, a plain UNAVAILABLE or another status without the service's ErrorInfo) and every earlier one first finishing through the chain, re-sent chained with no_wait until acknowledged; with that ErrorInfo (INVALID_UPDATE) the refusal is definitive. Acknowledgments settle in any order, collide outside chain order, and hold the positions an unsettled write may hold, a cancelled attempt's included. A chain refusal, an unknown outcome, a refusal that applied nothing or UNAUTHENTICATED breaks the chain: the chained calls of later writes are cancelled and not waited for, a status that does not settle the call is an unknown outcome, a re-send of a write of unknown outcome refused ALREADY_EXISTS, OBJECT_REPLACED or NOT_FOUND being final; while a queued write's outcome is unknown the read stays closed and the write is re-sent through the chain until it is acknowledged or the chain proves it committed, a refusal settling no later write of unknown outcome; a write the chain proves committed gets no inferred position: once settling ends the read is resubscribed from the coverage frontier, its catch-up applies in service order, this writer's commits included, and the write's intent retires with its proving write's application; an acknowledged or chain-proven write a net-empty catch-up passes retires without applying; a header-only frame after the catch-up target is an empty commit, and an aggregate of a resumed read retires the earlier read's peer coverage it contains; and every later write is re-sent unchanged at once, the first alone and with no_wait, the latest of unknown outcome first, with no_wait, while nothing locates the chain; a refusal names the writer's latest write by last_record and last_operation_id, and one naming a write the writer never issued, such as one without an operation ID or an admitted write not yet issued, or one earlier than a proven prefix, fails the layer OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. Admitted writes never exceed the window, one write without chaining, and at most one waits to be issued; otherwise host turns coalesce into one update of whole turns, compiled once when a slot frees, split into the most whole turns that fit when they exceed a compile limit together.
contracts.coverage_limit: Qualified only against the reference service's model of the proposed chained UpdateLayer, which no deployed service implements and which does not model replicas, the per-object writer limit or internal commit retries. The scene reference's catch-up is per commit for opaque layers and one aggregate for graph layers; the reconnect orderings of the progress model's scenario matrix (a lost reply and the loss of the read in either order, a stale attempt, a peer's identical edit, a peer undoing a lost write, aggregates and empty commits around lost writes, resubscription after a chain proof) are covered by the progress model alone; the scene reference covers a lost reply and read settled before a net-empty catch-up, a chain-proven write delivered by a resubscribed read's aggregate, and a plain status on a chained write settled through the chain. Window growth and the benchmark against omni-spectree are measured outside these lanes.

contracts.requirement: The reference service implements the proposed chained UpdateLayer: a chained_header requires operation_id and client_id before any chunk is read, every INVALID_ARGUMENT it gives a recognized chained call carries ErrorInfo INVALID_UPDATE, and a service without chaining or a pre-chaining replica refuses it INVALID_ARGUMENT without ErrorInfo before any chunk; Ping reports operation_ids and chained_writes; at the commit step the writer's own committed operation answers ALREADY_COMMITTED, a latest write equal to the predecessor (an absent record matching empty) commits and moves the record, and otherwise the call waits without blocking its predecessor or other writers until it can commit, a cancellation, which drops it with nothing applied, or its deadline, or under no_wait not at all, then applies nothing and fails ABORTED with ErrorInfo PREDECESSOR_NOT_COMMITTED naming the writer's latest write by last_record (absent, operation or no_operation_id) and last_operation_id; a replaced object fails FAILED_PRECONDITION and starts without records; unchained calls are unchanged; deterministic write faults refuse with nothing applied (ErrorInfo and RetryInfo), drop or hold a reply, hold a commit, let a stale call commit late and model a store restore that loses every record
contracts.coverage_limit: A model of a proposed live edit service change that no deployed service implements. One process serializes commit steps under one lock, so out-of-order arrival on different replicas, the per-object limit of 16 concurrent writers and internal commit retries are not modeled. A waiting call is refused ahead of its deadline, by half the remaining time and at most 0.5 s, so that the client receives the refusal; a stale commit step that runs after its call was answered checks its predecessor as a no_wait call does.
